report.summary: This frame is at Address with a technically sound setup: spine angle, shoulder line, and hip positions fall within typical pro ranges. Maintain the current posture and balance — the setup is solid for a good, repeatable swing.
coaching_recommendations: Reinforce your athletic spine angle by using the club-on-ground drill: place a club perpendicular to the target line and ensure your hands sit about a hand’s width above it to avoid over-bending (from p1_address_faults.md).

Keep weight centered on the balls of your feet — check balance with the heel-lift drill (briefly raise both heels in address). If you can’t lift, shift slightly more forward onto the toes to maintain an athletic stance (from p1_address_faults.md).

report.summary: Frame is a clear Toe-up position (classifier confidence 0.999). Overall the setup at P2 is largely within pro ranges — spine angle and hips look typical; there is a mild increase in right-shoulder rotation compared with the pro p25–p75 band but this is a small deviation, not a major fault. Given the prior Address was good, there’s no obvious sign that this mild shoulder difference is a carry-over problem from the setup.
coaching_recommendations: Use a one-piece takeaway: start the backswing by moving shoulders, arms and club together for the first ~1 foot to keep the club on a cleaner path. Drill (from corpus): place an alignment rod along the target line and practice sweeping the clubhead along that rod for the first ~18 inches.

Check grip neutrality and allow forearm rotation to follow the body turn rather than forcing the hands. The retrieved material recommends a neutral grip combined with a natural forearm rotation to reduce early face manipulation.

Practice slow, body-led takeaways (slow-motion reps) focusing on turning the torso rather than initiating with the hands; this encourages the shoulders and arms to work as a unit and helps prevent an inside or overly hand-driven takeaway.

report.summary: This frame shows a technically sound mid‑backswing: shoulders, hips and spine are all within typical pro ranges. The only measurable deviation is a mild shoulder-line tilt; there’s no clear evidence here that this is propagating from the earlier toe‑up observation at Address/Toe‑up.
coaching_recommendations: Prioritize rotating the torso rather than lifting with the arms — make half‑swings where the feeling is that the hands stay lower and the shoulders do the lifting (this helps avoid an outside/over‑the‑top path).

Use a tactile drill to preserve lead‑arm width: place a pool noodle or similar over the lead arm while making backswings so the arm is prevented from folding; this promotes an extended lead arm and wider arc.
Use a towel tucked under the trail (right) armpit during practice swings; keep the towel from falling out through the backswing to encourage connected rotation rather than arm lifting.

report.summary: This frame is classified as Top (99.97% confidence). Most measurements fall within typical pro ranges; the only measurable deviation is a mild reduction in left-hip rotation at the top, which is consistent with the earlier mid-backswing mild issues and suggests a slightly limited coil through the torso.
coaching_recommendations: Promote more hip rotation rather than compensatory upper-body tilt: practice slow backswings with one hand lightly on the trail hip, feeling the hip rotate backward (drill from 'Reverse spine angle' in p4_top_faults.md).

Maintain a connected trail arm to ensure a proper fold at the top: practice backswings with a headcover or glove tucked under the trail armpit — if it falls out the trail elbow has separated; keep the elbow "pocketed" toward the trail hip (from 'Flying trail elbow' in p4_top_faults.md).

Continue reinforcing the current shoulder turn and spine tilt — these are within typical pro ranges, so keep the same setup and rotation feel while applying the drills above (supporting text in p4_top_faults.md).

report.summary: The frame is confidently classified as Mid-downswing. Motion is generally sound but shows mild reduced hip rotation and a slightly larger-than-typical spine tilt at P5 — these are small deviations that can be related to the earlier mild issues you noted in the mid-backswing/top. Work on clearing the lead hip and sequencing the lower body before the arms to prevent these patterns from persisting.
coaching_recommendations: Cue and feel the lead hip clear: "clear the lead hip." Drill from the corpus: place an alignment stick alongside the lead hip and practice rotating the hip to touch the stick without sliding — this trains rotational clearance rather than lateral thrust (p5_middownswing_faults.md).

Start the downswing with the lower body: feel a small lead-hip "bump" toward the target before the arms move. Drill from the corpus: place a pool ball behind the trail knee and feel the knee move toward the ball before initiating the arms — this promotes correct sequencing and reduces being "stuck" at P5 (p5_middownswing_faults.md).

Use a quiet-posture check to prevent any unwanted standing-up: make slow downswings with your back lightly against a wall or chair. The corpus notes this immediately reveals any forward thrust of the hips and helps maintain spine angle through P5 (p5_middownswing_faults.md).

report.summary: This frame is Impact (high classifier confidence). The most notable issue is an over-open/right-shoulder angle at impact consistent with weight remaining on the trail side; this pattern can be connected to earlier mild issues in the backswing/top that leave the weight untransferred through the downswing. Shaft geometry data were unavailable, so I omitted shaft-specific feedback.

key_deviations.explanation: Right shoulder is rotated/opened substantially more than the pro range at impact, a pattern that matches a weight-on-trail (reverse pivot) presentation and reduces the ability to compress the ball.

coaching_recommendations: Address weight transfer through the downswing: practice the step-through drill (make impact with the trail foot raised) to force weight onto the lead side and rehearse a lead-side finish. (source: p6_impact_faults.md)

Prioritize hip rotation rather than hip thrust at impact: use the cue “belt buckle turns to face the target, not the ball,” and practice downswings against a wall behind the trail hip so any forward thrust is felt immediately. (source: p6_impact_faults.md)

report.summary: This frame shows a mild restriction in upper-body rotation through the mid-followthrough — the shoulder line and spine angle are slightly reduced compared with typical pro ranges. The pattern (mildly limited shoulder rotation) could be a continuation of the earlier impact-phase issues (notably the elevated right-shoulder at impact), suggesting some deceleration through and after impact rather than a full committed turn.
coaching_recommendations: Commit to finishing the swing: practice the cue from the corpus—"chase the ball with the club head"—to promote arm extension toward the target and prevent the arms folding early.

Drill 1 (no-ball full swings): make full practice swings without a ball, focusing on extending the arms out toward the target through P7 before allowing the body to wrap into the finish (this reinforces carrying momentum through impact).

Drill 2 (slow-motion followthrough): perform slow-motion followthroughs and check that the club toe reaches approximately vertical at P7 (toe pointing up), not past vertical; this helps reduce excessive forearm rotation and prevents a closed-face followthrough.

Check grip and lower-body rotation: verify a neutral grip and consciously continue lower-body rotation through impact so the hands do not over-rotate to compensate (both recommendations are from the retrieved mid-followthrough guidance).

report.summary: The finish shows incomplete lower-body rotation: the hips remain significantly closed to the target while the shoulders appear more open, indicating the lower body stalled through the follow-through. This is consistent with a common post-impact stall (hips stopping after impact) and may be a continuation of the swing issue noted at Impact; shaft-related feedback is omitted because the shaft proxy confidence is low.

key_deviations.explanation: Hips are under-rotated at the finish (belt buckle not facing the target), indicating the lower body stalled instead of continuing through to the target.

coaching_recommendations: Drive the hips all the way through so the belt-buckle/hip-line faces the target — cue: "turn your back pocket to the target." (Drill: check the finish after each swing; if the belt buckle is not facing the target, repeat the swing until it is.)

Make practice swings focusing on a high, committed finish with full rotation — think of the target, not the ball. (Drill: take slow, no-ball swings reaching a balanced finish, then replicate with a ball.)

Emphasize turning the torso before the arms: lead with your chest, not your hands. (Drill: practice full turns with just the torso/no club, then add the arms so the body carries the arms through the finish.)

synthesis.headline_summary: Setup is solid and repeatable, but the swing shows a clear weight-transfer and lower-body sequencing problem: weight remains too much on the trail side into impact (over-open right shoulder) and the hips stall through the finish. Earlier backswing/top frames show mild, non-severe limits in hip rotation that likely made it harder to sequence the downswing. Focus first on drills that force lead-side weight at impact (step-through) and drills/cues that drive the hips fully through the finish (belt-buckle/to-target finish and no-ball full swings).

priority_issues.issue_name: Insufficient lead-side weight transfer / open right shoulder at impact
priority_issues.explanation: At impact the right shoulder is substantially over-open (47.4°, well outside the pro band), indicating weight remained on the trail side through impact and reduced ability to compress the ball; mild reduced hip rotation and increased spine tilt seen in the mid-downswing and a mildly restricted rotation in the mid-followthrough are consistent contributors to this pattern.
priority_issues.primary_recommendation: Practice the step-through drill (make impact with the trail foot raised) to force weight onto the lead side and rehearse a lead-side finish, combined with the cue 'belt buckle turns to face the target' and downswings against a wall behind the trail hip to instantly feel and correct trail-side weight (sources: p6_impact_faults.md).

priority_issues.issue_name: Lower-body stall / under-rotated hips at finish
priority_issues.explanation: The finish shows significant under-rotation of the hips (right_hip 143.3° vs typical 158.7–167.2°), indicating the lower body stalled after impact rather than continuing to the target; this under-rotation is consistent with the impact-phase weight-on-trail pattern and reduces post-impact momentum and rotation through the shot.
priority_issues.primary_recommendation: Drive the hips fully through each swing — use the cue 'turn your back pocket to the target' and practice no-ball full swings focusing on a balanced, fully rotated finish (repeat swings until the belt buckle faces the target) as described in the finish guidance (sources: p8_finish_faults.md).

per_position_summary.Address: Setup at address is technically sound with athletic spine angle, shoulder line and hip positions within typical pro ranges.
per_position_summary.Toe-up: Toe-up (P2) shows a mild increase in right-shoulder rotation compared with the pro band but otherwise a normal takeaway.
per_position_summary.Mid-backswing: Mid-backswing is largely within pro ranges with only a mild shoulder-line tilt noted.
per_position_summary.Top: Top shows a mild reduction in left-hip rotation (slightly limited coil) while other measures remain near-pro.
per_position_summary.Mid-downswing: Mid-downswing presents mild reduced hip rotation and a slightly larger-than-typical spine tilt, suggesting limited lower-body clearance.
per_position_summary.Impact: Impact shows a notable over-open right-shoulder (47.4°), consistent with weight remaining on the trail side at impact (notable).
per_position_summary.Mid-followthrough: Mid-followthrough displays a mild restriction in upper-body rotation, consistent with some deceleration after impact.
per_position_summary.Finish: Finish reveals a notable lower-body stall with under-rotated hips (right_hip 143.3°), indicating the hips did not fully turn to the target (notable).

propagation_observations: Mildly limited hip rotation at the Top and mild reduced hip rotation/larger spine tilt at the Mid-downswing likely made it harder to clear the lower body, contributing to the trail-weight/open-shoulder presentation at Impact.

The open right-shoulder at Impact and the mild deceleration through the mid-followthrough appear to continue into the Finish as an under-rotated hip-line, indicating the problem persists through impact into the follow-through rather than being a single-frame event.

beginner_report.encouragement: Your setup is solid and repeatable, and your backswing and top positions are largely close to where we want them — that’s a great foundation to build from. With a few simple drills to move your weight onto the front foot and finish your hips through the shot, you’ll get more consistent contact and more power.

top_3_takeaways.title: Shift weight to front
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel like you’re stepping toward the target so most of your weight is on your front leg at impact — imagine landing softly on that front foot.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: Do the step-through drill: make controlled half‑swings and after contact lift or step forward with your back foot so you finish with most weight on the front foot, repeating until it feels natural.

top_3_takeaways.title: Turn hips all the way
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel your belt buckle and back pocket turning to point at the target and keep turning through the shot instead of stopping right after impact.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: Practice no‑ball full swings where you focus on rotating your hips through to a balanced finish with the belt buckle facing the target, repeating until you can hold that finish.

top_3_takeaways.title: Start hips before hands
top_3_takeaways.feel_cue: Feel a small, deliberate hip turn that leads the downswing — like your lower body gently pulls the rest of you through while your arms stay relaxed.
top_3_takeaways.simple_drill: From the top, make slow‑motion swings where you pause and then begin the downswing by turning your hips toward the target a split second before your hands and club follow.

beginner_report.one_sentence_summary: Good setup and backswing, but you tend to hang back through impact and not fully turn your hips — practice stepping through to the front foot and finishing with your belt buckle to the target.
